{{Short description|Twisted spin group}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Spin<sup>c</sup> group}}

In [[spin geometry]], a '''spin<sup>c</sup> group''' (or '''complex spin group''') is a [[Lie group]] obtained by the [[spin group]] through twisting with the first [[unitary group]]. C stands for the [[complex number]]s, which are denoted <math>\mathbb{C}</math>. An important application of spin<sup>c</sup> groups is for [[Spinc structure|spin<sup>c</sup> structures]], which are central for [[Seiberg–Witten theory]].

== Definition ==
The [[spin group]] <math>\operatorname{Spin}(n)</math> is a [[Double cover (topology)|double cover]] of the [[special orthogonal group]] <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math>, hence <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math> acts on it with <math>\operatorname{Spin}(n)/\Z_2\cong\operatorname{SO}(n)</math>. Furthermore, <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math> also acts on the first unitary group <math>\operatorname{U}(1)</math> through the [[Antipodal point|antipodal]] identification <math>y\sim -y</math>. The ''spin<sup>c</sup> group'' is then:<ref>Lawson & Michelson 1989, Appendix D, Equation (D.1)</ref><ref>Bär 1999, page 14</ref><ref>''Stable complex and Spin<sup>c</sup>-structures'', section 2.1</ref><ref>Nicolaescu, page 30</ref>

: <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(n)
:=\left(
\operatorname{Spin}(n)\times\operatorname{U}(1)
\right)/\mathbb{Z}_2
</math>

with <math>(x,y)\sim(-x,-y)</math>. It is also denoted <math>\operatorname{Spin}^\mathbb{C}(n)</math>. Using the exceptional isomorphism <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(2)
\cong\operatorname{U}(1)
</math>, one also has <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(n)
=\operatorname{Spin}^2(n)
</math> with:

: <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^k(n)
:=\left(
\operatorname{Spin}(n)\times\operatorname{Spin}(k)
\right)/\mathbb{Z}_2.
</math>

== Low-dimensional examples ==

* <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(1)
\cong\operatorname{U}(1)
\cong\operatorname{SO}(2)
</math>, induced by the isomorphism <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(1)
\cong\operatorname{O}(1)
\cong\mathbb{Z}_2
</math>
* <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(3)
\cong\operatorname{U}(2)
</math>,<ref>Nicolaescu, Exercise 1.3.9</ref> induced by the [[exceptional isomorphism]] <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(3)
\cong\operatorname{Sp}(1)
\cong\operatorname{SU}(2)
</math>. Since furthermore <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(2)
\cong\operatorname{U}(1)
\cong\operatorname{SO}(2)
</math>, one also has <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(3)
\cong\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{h}(2)
</math>.
* <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(4)
\cong\operatorname{U}(2)\times_{\operatorname{U}(1)}\operatorname{U}(2)
</math>, induced by the exceptional isomorphism <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(4)
\cong\operatorname{SU}(2)\times\operatorname{SU}(2)
</math>
* <math>
\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(6)
\rightarrow\operatorname{U}(4)
</math> is a double cover, induced by the exceptional isomorphism <math>
\operatorname{Spin}(6)
\cong\operatorname{SU}(4)
</math>

== Properties ==
For all higher abelian [[homotopy group]]s, one has:

: <math>
\pi_k\operatorname{Spin}^\mathrm{c}(n)
\cong\pi_k\operatorname{Spin}(n)\times\pi_k\operatorname{U}(1)
\cong\pi_k\operatorname{SO}(n)
</math>

for <math>
k\geq 2
</math>.
